title: Grateful Dead Live at DuPont Gym - MIT on 1970-05-07
source: this is a remaster of shnid 5439

ai_review.summary: A listenable restored audience tape of the May 7‑1970 MIT show delivers an epic Love Light medley and standout Easy Wind, despite occasional pitch quirks.
ai_review.review: This three‑set, 23‑song performance is praised for its long acoustic set, fluid Lovelight jam suite, and high‑energy numbers like Easy Wind, Candyman and Good Lovin'. The audience recording, cleaned up by SirMick, is clear enough for the era but still shows some EQ issues, mic chatter and pitch fluctuations that require a bit of forgiveness. Overall the show is considered a historic highlight of spring ’70 with many memorable moments.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance highly (standout songs, strong set flow) while noting only moderate recording flaws; weighted average yields a solid 4‑plus rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Cleaned up by SirMick; generally clear for the era but includes EQ adjustments, occasional mic chatter, pitch fluctuations and minor glitches in the first set.

poor_songs: The Other One (split into four tracks, editing issue)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A sprawling three‑set setlist with a lengthy acoustic portion and an adventurous second‑set jam marathon; praised for fluid transitions despite the typical unevenness of ’70 shows.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s humor is noted (jokes about “The Eleven” and “Phil Spector”), and his guitar work is implied to be strong throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s drumming gets a shout‑out for calling beats on "Beat It On Down the Line" and driving the rhythmic intensity.
